articles.excerpt: Lee Cartledge, 42, faces four charges following a vehicle stop in Middleton on Wednesday 11 November, Greater Manchester Police said.

Cartledge is due to appear at Manchester and Salford Magistrates’ Court on Thursday 12 November, according to the police statement issued that morning.

articles.title: Police search for man who helped woman after alleged sexual assault in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Greater Manchester Police are appealing for information regarding a man who assisted a woman following an alleged sexual assault in Rochdale town centre.
articles.content_html:
Greater Manchester Police are searching for a man who helped a woman following an alleged sexual assault in Rochdale town centre. The incident reportedly occurred at around 4.20am on Saturday, 16 May, in the King Street car park.

Officers stated that the man approached the woman and assisted her in getting home after the incident. Police believe he could be a key witness in their investigation and have issued a social media appeal to identify him.

Police said: "We are looking to identify the man that helped the woman and assisted her in getting home."

The witness was driving a silver Volkswagen Polo and left the scene in the direction of Halifax Road. Police have shared CCTV footage of the vehicle, although they acknowledged the quality is not ideal.

They are urging anyone who recognises the car or has information to come forward.

Anyone with information can contact Greater Manchester Police on 0161 856 4668, quoting the crime reference number CRI/06QQ/0010216/26. Alternatively, information can be submitted online or anonymously through Crimestoppers at 0800 555 111.

articles.title: Man arrested after suspected air pistol found near Rochdale Armistice Day ceremony
articles.excerpt: A 39-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of possessing an imitation firearm after police found what they believe is an air pistol near the Armistice Day ceremony in Rochdale town centre.
articles.content_html:
A 39-year-old man has been arrested after police found what they believe to be an air pistol near the Armistice Day remembrance ceremony in Rochdale town centre on Wednesday 11 November 2026.

Greater Manchester Police said officers approached the man at about 11.30am after he appeared to be protesting near the ceremony.

Officers said they had reasonable grounds to search him and found what is believed to be an air pistol.

He was arrested on suspicion of possession of an imitation firearm and remains in custody while enquiries continue.

Police said no injuries have been reported and there is currently no evidence that the air pistol was fired.

Police also confirmed that the man did not interrupt the service and was standing some distance from the main ceremony.

articles.title: Rochdale man who managed 'Adam' drug line dealers jailed for 10 and a half years
articles.excerpt: Haider Ali, 34, of Pike Street, was sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court on Monday 9 November after an investigation that began with a drug deal on Baron Street.
articles.content_html:
A Rochdale man who rose from street dealer to manager in the organised crime group behind the borough's 'Adam' drug line has been jailed for 10 years and six months.

Haider Ali, 34, of Pike Street, Rochdale, was sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court on Monday 9 November 2026.

He was sentenced for being concerned in the supply of cocaine and of heroin, and two counts each of possession with intent to supply cocaine and heroin, covering September 2024 to March 2025.

The investigation by GMP's Rochdale Challenger Unit began after police received information that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked on Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on 4 January 2025.

Officers followed the vehicle and carried out a reinforced stop when it pulled into a local petrol station. Ali, a passenger, got out and walked quickly away before he was detained.

He was found with more than £1,000 in cash and two mobile phones, which were seized.

In custody, officers recovered two bundles of wraps containing a brown and a white substance, later confirmed as heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid phone taken from him was confirmed to be the Adam drug line.

Investigators found Ali was not only dealing at street level but managing other street dealers, the dedicated dealer phone, and where those below him should make their next deal.

A warrant was executed at his home on 27 March 2025, when he was arrested again on suspicion of possession with intent to supply class A drugs and being concerned in their supply.

PC Joe Cooke, of GMP's Rochdale Challenger Unit, said: “The ‘Adam’ Organised Crime Group have caused misery for many years to the residents and communities of Rochdale and beyond. Haider Ali’s drug dealing as part of this OCG and his management of lower-level street dealers has contributed significantly to the success of the Adam OCG.”

He added: “Organised criminals such as Haider Ali are dangerous individuals with no remorse for their criminality. They operate to exploit the most vulnerable in our societies in order to increase their financial gain and notoriety.”

According to police, evidence showed Ali had progressed from street dealing in 2014 to a significant role within the Adam group by 2024 and into 2025.

Concerns about drug dealing can be reported to GMP on 101 or online at www.gmp.police.uk, or anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Source: Greater Manchester Police press release supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: Greater Manchester Police.

articles.title: Police warn Rochdale homes to lock away family gold after rise in burglaries
articles.excerpt: Burglaries targeting family gold have risen in Rochdale, Oldham and Bury in recent weeks, mostly at weekends, with entry usually gained at the rear of homes.
articles.content_html:
Police are urging Rochdale households to lock away family gold and jewellery after a rise in burglaries targeting it in Rochdale, Oldham and Bury in recent weeks.

Greater Manchester Police said the burglaries have mostly taken place at weekends, during the late afternoon and at night, and warned that offences are likely to increase as the darker nights draw in.

Burglars have most often got in by snapping or tampering with locks or by smashing their way in, while some properties were entered because they had been left insecure.

Entry is typically gained at the rear of the property. Police believe the offenders' vehicle is usually parked on streets surrounding the targeted home.

Detective Chief Inspector Roger Smethurst, of GMP's Serious Crime Division, said: "I would like to remind the public to stay vigilant as the darker nights draw in and ensure their property is secure.

"Anyone with expensive jewellery in their homes should ensure it is safely locked away, out of sight, purchasing a good quality safe which complies with insurance rating standards."

The warning comes as GMP reports that it has been the country's top force for solving residential burglaries over the last 12 months.

The force said 14.3% of residential burglaries so far this year have been solved, up from 9.5% the previous year.

In August 2026 alone, 15.9% of residential burglary outcomes were solved, compared with 9.8% in August 2025, according to GMP.

Crime prevention advice is available on the Greater Manchester Police website, gmp.police.uk.

Suspicious activity or information can be reported to GMP on 101, or anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Source: Greater Manchester Police, supplied to Rochdale Daily. Photograph: Greater Manchester Police (stock image).

articles.title: Drunk driver jailed after Rochdale police pursuit left pedestrian with life-changing injuries
articles.excerpt: Cameron Grainger fled officers through Rochdale town centre after a night drinking. A man was seriously injured when he was struck by the police car trying to stop him.
articles.content_html:
A man who led police on a pursuit through Rochdale after an evening of drinking has been jailed for more than four years.

Cameron Grainger was found guilty of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court today (Friday 6 November), Greater Manchester Police said. He was also banned from driving for six years and two months.

The court heard that at about 1am on Sunday 19 November 2023, Grainger parked his Seat Leon in the Upper Broadfield car park in Rochdale town centre and spent almost three hours in bars and pubs nearby with three friends.

CCTV operators watching the town centre saw him return to the car at around 3.25am and alerted police that a man who appeared intoxicated was about to drive away. Officers were given a description of the car, its registration and where it was leaving from.

When officers tried to stop the car as it left the town centre, Grainger failed to stop. CCTV showed him driving at speed along Rochdale Road and on the wrong side of the road throughout.

The pursuit ended when a man, now 41, was struck by the police car as officers tried to bring Grainger to a stop. Officers stopped to give him first aid at the scene. GMP said his injuries have changed his life.

Grainger kept driving before abandoning the car on Wellington Street, where CCTV captured him and his three passengers running from it. He was arrested the next day, gave no comment in interview, and was found not to be insured to drive the car. The court ordered the Seat Leon to be destroyed.

One of the passengers, Teagan Clements, later gave police a false statement. She was given a 20-week prison sentence, suspended for 18 months, and 80 hours of unpaid work for making a false statement tendered in evidence.

Detective Sergeant Louise Warhurst, of GMP’s Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said Grainger had consciously chosen to drive after drinking, and that the injured man’s life had been fundamentally changed.

“This case serves as a stark reminder of the potentially life-changing consequences of drink-driving,” she said.

GMP’s release gives the prison term as “four years and five” without completing the figure. Rochdale Daily has asked the press office to confirm the full term and will update this report.

articles.title: Greater Manchester Police to host pop-up fraud prevention events in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: In a bid to protect shoppers from online fraud, Greater Manchester Police will hold pop-up events in Rochdale next week, providing essential advice and support.
articles.content_html:
In the lead-up to Christmas, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) is organising pop-up fraud-prevention events in Rochdale to help shoppers avoid online scams.

The sessions will take place at Virgin Money on Yorkshire Street on Tuesday 10 November, and at Halifax on the same street on Wednesday 11 November, both from 10am to 1pm.

The events are being hosted by GMP’s Economic Crime Unit, which aims to educate the public about the various types of scams, from simple confidence tricks to sophisticated online fraud.

Attendees will have the opportunity to speak with police staff and volunteers about any concerns they may have regarding fraud and cyber crime.

GMP has emphasised the importance of staying informed about the latest scams and has provided tips to reduce the risk of becoming a victim.

These include never sharing passwords or personal details, regularly updating devices and apps, and ensuring that emails and attachments are only opened if they come from trusted sources.

These pop-up events are crucial as they provide direct access to expert advice and support for local residents, particularly during the busy shopping season. By attending, shoppers can better protect themselves from potential scams and ensure a safer festive period.

articles.title: Middleton residents warned about scammers posing as council officials
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has issued a warning to residents in Middleton about scammers posing as council officials to gain entry into homes.
articles.content_html:
Residents in Middleton are being warned about scammers posing as council officials in an attempt to gain entry into their homes. This warning follows reports of several incidents in the area, prompting Rochdale Council to take action.

The council stated, "We have been made aware of bogus cold callers posing as council officers to gain entry into homes." They emphasised that all legitimate council staff carry identification and can produce it upon request.

Residents are advised to check for ID before allowing anyone into their homes.

If residents are unsure about a caller's identity or if they cannot produce an official badge, they are encouraged to refuse entry.

The council also reminded residents that services and appointments can only be booked and paid for in advance through their contact centre at 01706 647474.

Residents who have experienced similar visits are urged to report them to Greater Manchester Police, either online or by calling 101.

The council shared: “We have been made aware of bogus cold callers posing as council officers to gain entry into homes. “We want to advise residents that all council staff carry council ID and will be able to produce this upon request. “Council staff will be able to show this before you allow them entry. If in doubt, or if an official badge cannot be produced, you can refuse entry. “Services and appointments can only be booked and paid for in advance through our contact centre. “If you are not sure about a caller then please get in touch on 01706 647474. “If you have received a similar visit, especially in the Middleton area, please report it to Greater Manchester Police either online or through 101.” While many cold callers are legitimate salespeople, rogue traders also use cold calling to scam customers into handing over their money or personal details. The council’s advice is to always lock your doors, even when you are at home. READ MORE: Warning as measles cases are confirmed If an unexpected caller knocks on the door and you decide to open it, make sure all other doors and access points are locked so no one can get in while you’re distracted. If the caller wants to come in, always check their identity first, even if you were expecting somebody to visit. If you’re unsure if the person is a legitimate caller, call their head office using the number from a recent bill, email or website. The goods and services offered by rogue traders can range from prize draws to psychic letters. Do not give out personal details or bank information unless absolutely necessary. Scammers can use details they already have to convince you they are legitimate and trick you into giving them more information. Warning signs that a salesperson isn’t legitimate include pressuring you to make a purchase or responding to the offer straight away. If you are asked to make a purchase to win a prize or call a premium rate number to claim an offer, it is likely to be a scam. A salesperson not wanting to give their address or contact details, or asking for your bank details are other red flags. If you pay or agree to pay over £42 for any goods or services on the doorstep, you have 14 days to cancel the agreement without penalty and be fully refunded. Cold callers must give you written information on your cancellation rights or the agreement isn’t valid. It is illegal for a trader to force you to sign away your cancellation rights. articles.title: Six vehicles seized during road safety operation in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Police seized six vehicles, including an e-scooter, during a road safety operation in Rochdale, with multiple drivers reported for various offences.
articles.content_html:
Police seized six vehicles during a road safety operation in Rochdale on 4 November 2026. The operation involved officers from the Rochdale North and Rochdale East neighbourhood policing teams, alongside Greater Manchester Police’s traffic division and Rochdale Council’s Licensing and Trading Standards teams.

A total of 104 vehicles were stopped during the operation. Among the seized vehicles was an e-scooter.

One driver was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving, while 11 others were reported for having illegal number plates. Additional reports included one driver for not wearing a seat belt, another for driving without a licence, and two motorists for driving without insurance.

The operation aimed to enhance road safety in the area, with GMP Rochdale noting that while many drivers and vehicles were operating within the law, a small number were not. This initiative reflects ongoing efforts to ensure compliance with road safety regulations.

Following this operation, local residents may see increased police presence and enforcement on the roads. The community is encouraged to adhere to traffic laws to ensure safety for all road users.

articles.title: Banned driver leads police on high-speed chase through Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A banned driver was involved in a high-speed chase through Rochdale, raising concerns about road safety in the area.
articles.content_html:
A banned driver led police on a high-speed chase through Rochdale on Saturday afternoon. The pursuit involved multiple police units and caused significant disruption to local traffic on the A58.

No injuries were reported during the chase, which raised concerns among residents about road safety. Police reiterated their commitment to tackling dangerous driving in the area.

Local authorities are expected to review the incident as part of ongoing efforts to enhance road safety measures in Rochdale.

Residents are encouraged to report any reckless driving incidents to the police, contributing to a safer environment for all.

articles.title: Eighth arrest in property damage investigation covering Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Police have received 63 reports of damage to HMOs or properties mistaken for them across six Greater Manchester districts, including Rochdale. Eight arrests have been made and one person has been brought before court.
articles.content_html:
Police have received 63 reports of damage to properties across six Greater Manchester districts, including Rochdale, in an investigation that has led to eight arrests.

In an update issued on Friday 6 November, Greater Manchester Police said one person had been brought before the courts. The release did not identify that person or give details of the case.

The investigation concerns houses in multiple occupation, known as HMOs, and properties mistaken for HMOs. Reports have been received from Rochdale, Salford, Tameside, Stockport, Bolton and Wigan since the start of October.

The figure of 63 covers all six districts. Police have not given a separate Rochdale total or identified the properties affected in the borough.

The most recent arrest was made on Monday 2 November. In its earlier announcement, GMP said a 29-year-old man had been arrested that morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage. The force did not state where that arrest took place.

Chief Superintendent Marcus Noden said officers had been working with partner organisations across Greater Manchester to understand the damage and respond.

He said: “Our investigation has led to eight people being brought into our custody so far and, since making the latest arrest, we've seen three further reports of similar damage.”

He added: “You will continue to see our officers in areas that have been affected by this criminality as we continue our enforcement action.”

Police are continuing to appeal for information. Anyone who can help can call 101 or report information online at https://www.gmp.police.uk/.

Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

No finding of guilt should be inferred from an arrest or court appearance. Anyone accused is presumed innocent unless and until convicted.

articles.title: Rochdale driver jailed for 16 months after dangerous police pursuit
articles.excerpt: Bilal Ishaq admitted four driving offences after a pursuit through Rochdale. Police say he ran red lights and twice tried to reverse into pursuing vehicles.
articles.content_html:
A disqualified driver who fled police through Rochdale has been jailed for 16 months and banned from driving for five years.

Bilal Ishaq, 34, of Hey Street, Rochdale, pleaded guilty to dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, failing to stop and driving without insurance, Greater Manchester Police said in a release issued on 2 November.

Officers had tried to stop a vehicle on Foxholes Road in September. GMP said the vehicle was linked to suspected drug dealing. The offences set out in the force’s sentencing announcement were driving offences.

Ishaq drove away, beginning a pursuit through the town. According to police, he reached speeds more than three times the limit, went through red lights and drove on the wrong side of the road.

The force said he also tried to reverse into pursuing police vehicles on two occasions. After crashing, he attempted to run away but was detained by officers.

GMP said Ishaq was already subject to two driving disqualifications imposed in January 2026 following a separate dangerous driving incident in December 2025.

PC Matt Balkwell, from the force’s Motorcycle Unit, said: “His actions could easily have resulted in serious injury or loss of life.”

The officer praised the work of those involved in detaining Ishaq and said police would continue to pursue drivers who endangered their communities.

articles.title: Former police officer sacked for sharing confidential information with Rochdale drug dealer
articles.excerpt: Tubah Hamid, a former Tameside police officer, was dismissed after breaching confidentiality by sharing police information with her Rochdale drug dealer partner.
articles.content_html:
Tubah Hamid, a former police officer with Greater Manchester Police, was dismissed after an accelerated misconduct hearing found she had shared confidential police information with her partner, who is linked to an organised crime group in Rochdale.

The hearing, presided over by Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson, concluded that Hamid's actions constituted gross misconduct due to multiple breaches of professional standards.

The misconduct hearing revealed that Hamid's behaviour included unlawful access to police data over an extended period, which was described as 'deliberate and persistent'. Sir Stephen stated that her culpability was 'very high', highlighting a significant abuse of her position and a lack of integrity.

As a result of her actions, Hamid was dismissed with immediate effect and her name has been added to the College of Policing's Barred List, preventing her from serving in any police role in the future.

The disciplinary proceedings followed a criminal investigation into her conduct, which raised serious concerns about her suitability for the role of constable.

The dismissal of Tubah Hamid serves as a significant reminder of the consequences of misconduct within law enforcement.

articles.title: Police arrest 17 in operation against crime gang in Rochdale and Heywood
articles.excerpt: Seventeen arrests were made during a police operation targeting an organised crime group linked to violence in Heywood earlier this year.
articles.content_html:
Seventeen people have been arrested as police tackle an organised crime group in Rochdale and Heywood. This operation, named Operation Rivercrest, involved 250 officers executing a series of raids across multiple locations, including Rochdale, Heywood, Bury, Salford, Manchester, Merseyside, and Yorkshire.

The arrests, which took place on the morning of 27 October 2026, included sixteen men aged between 19 and 49, who are suspected of various offences such as drug supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery.

A 21-year-old woman was also arrested on suspicion of being involved in drug supply.

Detective Sergeant Hannah Taala from Greater Manchester Police’s Rochdale Division stated that the operation was initiated following a violent incident in Heywood earlier this year, which resulted in serious injuries and the use of weapons, including machetes.

A cannabis farm was discovered during the raids, further highlighting the extent of the criminal activities.

The police's focus on this crime group aims to disrupt their operations and enhance community safety. The investigation is ongoing, and further updates are expected as the police continue to address the issues surrounding organised crime in the area.

People are frightened, people don’t want to provide statements when they’ve witnessed something. “We understand that they don’t want to do that and they don’t want to get involved, but we’re always there to listen, to speak to them if they’ve got any concerns.” DS Taala said the exploitation of vulnerable by organised crime gangs was a particular issue police are keen to tackle. Now, people are more aware of what that is. “We tend to get more calls about people being concerned and we’re trying to focus on that and actually go out into the community to speak to people and to understand exactly what’s going on and we’re trying to proactively deal with that.” One of the aims of today’s operation is to reassure the community that the police are taking the issue seriously DS Taala said: “The community needs to know that we are doing something — we won’t stand for this in our community. “People sometimes think we’re not doing anything because they don’t see us out there and tackling it as it happens. We try to proactively police areas but we can’t always be aware of what’s going happen. “We are investigating, and we have their best interests at heart. We don’t want people living in fear in the community so we want to tackle organised crime. Police discovered evidence of drug dealing. Image: GMP “We’ve taken the first step in getting our target nominals today, and there will be more investigations come. We’re gathering evidence that may take us further afield. It doesn’t stop here. “Every step of an investigation opens up another can of worms, and we keep going, and we keep going. “But at the minute, we’re focussing on what’s happening within our division of Rochdale.” DS Taala also appealed to people who have become caught up in an organised crime gang. “I have an issue with people taking advantage of vulnerable people, especially. “People need to understand the never in too deep. People sometimes feel like they’ve got themselves into a situation you can’t get out of and they don’t want to contact us because they think it’s too late or they’ve been involved along the way and they’re now being exploited. “We will always listen to them. It doesn’t matter if they think we’re going to judge them, or if they think they’re going to get in trouble. “We’re always here, and willing to listen, not just to the people that are being exploited, but also to people that are concerned about them.” Warrants were executed this morning. articles.title: Teenager jailed for fatal crash in Middleton after teaching himself to drive
articles.excerpt: An 18-year-old has been sentenced to nearly seven years in prison after causing the death of a grandfather in Middleton while driving unlicensed and recklessly.
articles.content_html:
A teenager has been sentenced to nearly seven years in prison for causing the death of a grandfather in Middleton while driving unlicensed and recklessly. Ruhul Islam, now 18, taught himself to drive by watching YouTube videos and was behind the wheel of his brother's Nissan Micra when he struck Terence James, 78, on Shawbury Street on 29 September 2024.

During a hearing at Manchester Crown Court on 13 October 2026, it was revealed that Islam had borrowed the car to make takeaway deliveries for a local business. Witnesses reported seeing him swerving through traffic, running red lights, and driving aggressively shortly before the crash.

Mr James was crossing the road with his 10-year-old granddaughter when he was hit, suffering severe injuries that led to his death the following day after life support was withdrawn.

Judge Kate Cornell described the vehicle as a 'dangerous weapon' in the hands of someone unqualified to drive. She stated that Mr James would likely still be alive had Islam adhered to traffic laws.

The court heard that Islam initially attempted to conceal his involvement in the crash, claiming his older brother was driving at the time.

Following the sentencing, it is expected that discussions around stricter enforcement of driving regulations may take place, although no specific measures have been announced yet.

articles.title: New Support Website Launched for Survivors of Child Sexual Abuse in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A new website, IAmReady.org, offers tailored support for survivors of child sexual abuse and exploitation, providing resources to help them navigate investigations and review closed cases.
articles.content_html:
Survivors of child sexual abuse and exploitation in Rochdale can now access a new support service designed to help them understand their options regarding investigations into their allegations. The website, IAmReady.org, offers tailored advice and guidance based on individual needs, enabling victims to make informed decisions about their cases.

Developed in collaboration with survivors, the website provides trauma-informed information in an accessible format. Users can navigate the site at their own pace, with features that allow them to save their progress and exit quickly for privacy. The platform also includes options for users to request a review of their cases if they were previously closed by the Crown Prosecution Service or local police, particularly under the Victims’ Right to Review (VRR) or the Child Sexual Abuse Review Panel (CSARP).

This initiative is part of Operation Beaconport, which was established in November 2025 following Baroness Casey’s audit of group-based child sexual abuse and exploitation. The operation is currently reviewing hundreds of cases where no further action was taken between 1 January 2010, and 31 March 2025. Victims wishing to submit information about previously closed cases involving group-based offending will have their requests reviewed by specially trained officers from the operation.

The launch of IAmReady.org aims to empower survivors by providing them with the necessary tools and support to navigate their experiences and seek justice. For those affected, this resource may represent a significant step towards healing and accountability.

articles.title: Milnrow woman's appeal against Animal ban rejected by Court
articles.excerpt: A Milnrow woman has had her appeal against a five-year ban on keeping animals dismissed by a judge after her dog was put down due to untreated injuries.
articles.content_html:
A woman from Milnrow has had her appeal against a five-year ban on keeping animals rejected by a judge at Manchester Crown Court. Anne Marie Wood was previously sentenced for causing unnecessary suffering to her dog, Tilly, who had to be euthanised after suffering from a broken leg that went untreated.

The RSPCA received a tip-off in December 2024 regarding Tilly's condition and found the Bichon Frise visibly lame and hesitant to put weight on her front leg. Wood initially refused to cooperate with inspectors but eventually allowed them into her home.

She claimed the injury occurred when Tilly fell while being passed through a front window and stated that she could not afford the necessary veterinary treatment, which was estimated to be between £400 and £500.

Despite the RSPCA's offer to take Tilly to their Greater Manchester Animal Hospital for examination, Wood declined. When Tilly was eventually seen by a vet, it was determined that her injuries were severe and that treatment could not restore an acceptable quality of life.

The decision was made to put her to sleep to prevent further suffering.

Wood, of St James Street, pleaded guilty at Tameside Magistrates Court on 31 July and received an 18-month prison sentence, suspended for one year, along with a ten-day Rehabilitation Activity Requirement and a nine-month drug rehabilitation programme.

Following the rejection of her appeal on 30 September, Wood remains banned from keeping animals for five years.

articles.title: Boy, 13, stabbed in Rochdale town centre: six arrested, two bailed and stop-and-search powers extended
articles.excerpt: Live story. Six teenage boys have now been arrested after a 13-year-old was stabbed in Rochdale town centre on Saturday night. Two have been released on bail, four remain in custody, and Section 60 stop-and-search powers in the town centre run until 3pm on Tuesday. Updated as Greater Manchester Police confirm developments.
articles.content_html:
Latest, 08:30, Tuesday 1 September: six teenage boys have been arrested in connection with the stabbing of a 13-year-old boy in Rochdale town centre on Saturday night, 29 August. Two were arrested on Sunday and have since been released on bail. Four more were arrested on Monday and remain in custody. All six were held on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article, Greater Manchester Police said. The injured boy remains in hospital receiving treatment.

This is Rochdale Daily's single live story on the incident. It is updated in place, newest first, only when Greater Manchester Police or another primary source confirms a development. Earlier separate reports have been folded into this page; see the correction note at the foot.

What we know

The boy was stabbed during a serious assault in the town centre, near the Riverside shopping centre, on the evening of Saturday 29 August. Police described the incident as a serious assault alongside wider disorder in the town centre that night. He was taken to hospital, where he remains.

Monday 31 August: GMP confirmed four further arrests, all teenage boys, on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article. The two boys arrested on Sunday were released on bail while enquiries continue. Detective Superintendent Richard Hunt said the force was continuing to make progress on the investigation and that violence on the streets would not be tolerated.

Monday 31 August: the Section 60 order covering Rochdale town centre was extended until 3pm on Tuesday 1 September. Under Section 60 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act, officers can stop and search people in the designated area without needing reasonable suspicion.

Sunday 30 August: GMP announced two arrests and put a 24-hour Section 60 order in place for the town centre from 3pm. Chief Inspector Michael Barton, neighbourhoods lead for GMP's Rochdale district, said detectives were reviewing CCTV, gathering witness statements and analysing intelligence to identify everyone involved.

Saturday 29 August: a 13-year-old boy was stabbed in the town centre. GMP log 2750 of 29/08/2026.

What we do not know

Police have not released the boy's condition beyond confirming he remains in hospital, and have not said what led to the assault. No one has been charged. Rochdale Daily will not name anyone arrested and will not publish speculation about motive or identity while the investigation is live.

How to help the investigation

Anyone who witnessed the incident, was in Rochdale town centre on Saturday evening, or has mobile phone, CCTV or dashcam footage is asked to contact GMP on 101, quoting log 2750 of 29/08/2026, or via the LiveChat function at gmp.police.uk. Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

Story first published 30 August 2026 as "Two arrested following stabbing incident in Rochdale"; consolidated into this live page on 1 September 2026.

Nathan Haigh, 31, was found unresponsive inside an address on Great Howarth after emergency services were called at around 7.39pm on Tuesday 11 August. CPR was commenced, but he was pronounced dead shortly afterwards.

Police initially described the circumstances as suspicious and arrested a 37-year-old woman on suspicion of murder while several lines of enquiry were explored. The subsequent decision to rule out murder represents a substantive change in the status of the investigation.

articles.excerpt: LIVE updates after a 23-year-old Greater Manchester Police student officer was arrested on suspicion of rape, kidnap and dangerous driving following a pursuit on the M62.
articles.content_html:

18:50 — Greater Manchester Police says it is committed to working with the Crown Prosecution Service to bring the case to court as quickly as possible, while also accelerating misconduct proceedings within police regulations. Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said the allegations were deeply concerning and disturbing and said all necessary and decisive action would be taken in the interests of the woman and the public.

GMP has confirmed its Professional Standards Directorate carried out an initial review of the officer's vetting and found it had been completed without any reason for concern. The force stressed that this did not lessen the severity of the allegations.

18:42 — Rochdale Daily moved this breaking story to live coverage. We will add confirmed developments from Greater Manchester Police, the Independent Office for Police Conduct and other authoritative sources as they emerge.

WHAT WE KNOW SO FAR

A 23-year-old Greater Manchester Police student officer has been arrested on suspicion of rape and kidnap following a police pursuit on the M62.

The officer was off duty when a 999 call was received shortly before 10.20pm on Saturday. Police said a woman in her 20s could be heard in distress in a vehicle in the Manchester area.

Officers traced the suspect's personal vehicle and began a pursuit. The pursuit continued onto the M62 before the officer was detained in West Yorkshire.

The 23-year-old was arrested on suspicion of rape, kidnap and dangerous driving. GMP says he has been suspended from duty and remains in custody for questioning.

The woman is being supported by specialist officers and other agencies.

Greater Manchester Police has made a voluntary referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct. Internal misconduct proceedings are also being progressed.

Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said thousands of GMP officers and staff who work to protect the public would be shocked and angered by the allegations. He said specialist resources had been assigned to the investigation and gave a commitment that the force would work with prosecutors as the criminal investigation progresses.

The allegations have not been proven. An arrest does not amount to a finding of guilt and the officer is entitled to the presumption of innocence unless and until convicted. This live page will be updated when further information is confirmed.

The Strand is an important neighbourhood hub used by families, shoppers and people accessing local community facilities, and residents should be able to use the area without feeling intimidated or being subjected to abuse.

Begging itself and antisocial or abusive behaviour are not necessarily the same thing, and people experiencing homelessness or financial hardship should not automatically be treated as offenders. However, threatening, intimidating or verbally abusive behaviour can be reported to police, particularly where somebody feels unsafe.

The reported incident remains an allegation and Rochdale Daily is not identifying the man involved. No suggestion is made that he has committed a criminal offence unless and until police establish the circumstances and take any appropriate action.

articles.title: Fraudsters who fought over the pensioners they were fleecing jailed - Rochdale woman among victims of £97,000 scam
articles.excerpt: Eight people have been sentenced over a roofing scam that took £97,000 from five elderly victims in three months - including £7,800 from a 77-year-old Rochdale woman. Two victims died before seeing justice.
articles.content_html:
A group of fraudsters who squabbled over the vulnerable pensioners they were ripping off have been jailed - including for a scam that stripped £7,800 from a 77-year-old Rochdale woman.

Eight people have now been sentenced over a ruthless building scam that took around £97,000 from five elderly victims across England in the space of just three months. They pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud and related money laundering offences.

The fraudsters pressured pensioners into handing over cash, making bank transfers and signing large cheques for roof repairs that were never carried out.

The 77-year-old woman from Rochdale was pressured into handing over cash, making transfers and signing cheques totalling £7,800, forced to dip into savings to pay for work that was never done.

Some of the most disturbing details emerged when police examined messages recovered from the offenders' phones. Two rival groups of scammers had independently targeted the same vulnerable man in Ellesmere Port. They regularly took him to local cash machines and made him withdraw money, and also used his bank card to buy themselves food and groceries. As his money ran out, the two rival factions clashed over who had the right to keep defrauding him.

The offending only came to light when the man's regular direct debits started to bounce because his account had been drained, and he turned to a friend for help.

Other victims included an elderly man in Ellesmere Port persuaded to write cheques worth £34,500 for roof work that was never completed, an elderly woman in Coventry whose signed blank cheques were written out for £13,000, and an elderly woman in Corby who had unnecessary roof repairs carried out to a poor standard.

The stolen money was laundered through the bank accounts of several accomplices before being spent on expensive meals and luxury Rolex watches.

Tragically, two of the elderly victims died before the gang finally appeared in court and never saw justice served.

Detective Constable Rob Mackay, of Ellesmere Port CID, who led the investigation, described it as a lengthy and complex inquiry.

Trading standards advice is never to agree to work from a cold caller, to seek quotes from traders you approach yourself, and to talk to a trusted friend or family member before parting with money. Anyone who believes an elderly relative or neighbour is being targeted can contact police on 101, or Action Fraud.

articles.title: 60 police officer misconduct cases in a single year. To protect and serve?
articles.excerpt: A Rochdale Daily analysis of Greater Manchester Police's own published misconduct reports found 60 officer misconduct case entries in 2025 - with 41 ending in dismissal or a finding that dismissal would have followed.
articles.content_html:
The words "To Protect & Serve" represent one of the most recognisable ideals of modern policing. The overwhelming majority of police officers go to work every day to protect the public with professionalism and integrity.

But Greater Manchester Police's own published misconduct records reveal another side of policing that deserves public scrutiny.

An analysis by Rochdale Daily of GMP's published quarterly misconduct outcome reports found 60 police officer misconduct case entries during 2025.

Those cases involved allegations ranging from criminal convictions and violence to discriminatory behaviour, misuse of confidential police systems and failures to investigate serious offences.

Among the allegations recorded by GMP were: assault occasioning actual bodily harm; drink-driving convictions; positive drug tests, including cocaine; sexual assault; domestic abuse and coercive control allegations considered through misconduct proceedings; criminal damage; misuse of police computer systems; racist, misogynistic, homophobic and discriminatory messages; sexual harassment of colleagues; inappropriate contact with vulnerable members of the public; failures to investigate allegations of rape; and breaches of police business interest regulations.

The outcomes were equally striking.

Of the 60 officer misconduct case entries reviewed, 19 resulted in dismissal without notice. A further 22 resulted in findings that the officer would have been dismissed had they still been serving with Greater Manchester Police. Six resulted in final written warnings, five in written warnings, and two allegations were not proven. The remaining cases resulted in other disciplinary outcomes, including practice improvement or findings below the threshold for gross misconduct.

In other words, 41 of the 60 cases resulted in either dismissal or a finding that dismissal would have been the outcome had the officer remained in service.

Every misconduct case has its own facts and circumstances, and misconduct proceedings are separate from criminal court proceedings. Some officers had already resigned or retired before their hearings concluded, which is why some outcomes are recorded as "would have been dismissed."

It is also important to recognise that Greater Manchester Police employs thousands of officers. The misconduct cases published during 2025 represent a small proportion of the overall workforce, and the published reports do not suggest that misconduct is typical of policing within the force.

Nevertheless, policing relies on public confidence. Every misconduct finding, particularly those involving violence, dishonesty, discrimination, abuse of authority or failures to investigate serious crime, has the potential to undermine that trust.

Transparency matters.

That is why Rochdale Daily has launched Police Watch, an ongoing series examining police accountability using official records, misconduct decisions, court judgments, Freedom of Information responses and reports from independent oversight bodies.

This investigation is not about attacking policing. It is about ensuring that the public can see how misconduct is identified, investigated and dealt with when officers fall below the standards expected of them.

Methodology: This analysis is based on Greater Manchester Police's published quarterly misconduct outcome reports covering January to December 2025. The figure of 60 refers to police officer misconduct case entries published by GMP. Police staff cases were excluded from the analysis. Because some published cases are anonymised, the reports do not always allow confirmation that every entry relates to a different individual, and therefore the figure should be understood as the number of recorded officer misconduct cases rather than confirmed unique officers.

Sources: Greater Manchester Police's official published misconduct outcome reports - GMP Misconduct Outcomes, January to March 2025; April to June 2025; July to September 2025; and October to December 2025.

articles.title: Shabir Ahmed barred from Rochdale under strict licence conditions as government pushes to deport him
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale grooming gang ringleader is excluded from the borough under his licence conditions, is living under 24-hour supervision at an undisclosed location outside the area, and faces active government efforts to deport him.
articles.content_html:
Shabir Ahmed, the ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang jailed in 2012, was released from prison on licence on 2 July after serving 14 years of a 22-year sentence for multiple rape and sexual offences against young girls. Rochdale Daily can confirm, based on conditions set out by the Home Office and Ministry of Justice, that he is not living in Rochdale and is barred from entering the borough.

His licence conditions include an exclusion zone covering Rochdale and Oldham, electronic GPS tagging to monitor his movements, a requirement to live in approved accommodation staffed 24 hours a day, and a ban from his last known address in Oldham. The Ministry of Justice has said he is subject to the toughest supervision possible and would be returned to prison immediately if any condition were breached.

Ahmed, 73, was initially placed in approved premises in Accrington, Lancashire. After that address was shared on social media, prompting protests in the town and calls from the local MP for his removal, he was moved. The government has not confirmed his current location, and Rochdale Daily will not publish unverified claims about his whereabouts. Speculation of that kind has already forced one relocation and puts bystanders at the shared addresses at risk.

The question survivors and residents have pressed hardest is why he remains in the country at all. Ahmed was stripped of his British citizenship after his conviction, and victims had been led to believe he would be deported on release. It has since emerged that a provision of the Immigration Act 1971 prevents the removal of Commonwealth citizens who arrived in the United Kingdom before 1973, as Ahmed did as a teenager in 1967.

The government says it is exploring every option to remove him. Downing Street has confirmed talks with Pakistan, and a Home Office minister told the Commons that “all options are on the table”, saying the government would not give up its efforts given the nature of his crimes. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has set out plans to amend the 1971 Act so that people convicted of the most serious offences, including child sexual exploitation, can no longer rely on its protections, and ministers have indicated emergency legislation could be considered.

Pakistan, however, has publicly rejected the request. Officials in Islamabad have said responsibility for Ahmed lies with Britain, where he was brought up, and he is reported to have renounced his Pakistani citizenship, which complicates removal further even if the British law changes. The Prime Minister's spokesman has declined to comment on specific proposals while the talks continue.

The pressure on ministers is cross-party. The Conservatives have proposed amending the government's immigration legislation to close the loophole, with their leader urging ministers to adopt the change and the shadow home secretary suggesting visa sanctions or cuts to aid if Pakistan continues to refuse. Greater Manchester's mayor is among those who have called publicly for deportation, and the MP for Hyndburn, where Ahmed was first housed, has demanded he be barred from the North West entirely.

Campaigners including former Greater Manchester Police detective Maggie Oliver have criticised the handling of the release, saying victims learned of it through social media and continue to live with fear that the authorities have not taken seriously.

Rochdale Daily will update this article as official information is released. Readers should treat any claim about Ahmed's location that does not come from the Home Office, the Ministry of Justice, Greater Manchester Police or the courts as unverified.

articles.title: Kirkholt and the fight against knife crime: why prevention matters as much as policing
articles.excerpt: Knife crime remains a concern for many families in Kirkholt, but police, youth workers and community groups say prevention, education and opportunity are just as important as enforcement in keeping young people safe.
articles.content_html:
Knife crime remains one of the issues that concerns many families across Kirkholt and the wider Rochdale borough. While high-profile incidents often make headlines, community leaders, police and youth organisations all agree that preventing young people from carrying knives in the first place is just as important as enforcing the law against those who do.

Although Rochdale has lower levels of knife crime than several other parts of Greater Manchester, it continues to experience incidents involving bladed weapons, particularly in areas facing higher levels of deprivation. The borough's Strategic Threat Assessment notes that knife crime is more common in town centres and some residential neighbourhoods where poverty is greatest, while young people are disproportionately affected as both victims and offenders. It also found that some children told youth workers they carried knives because they believed it offered protection or improved their image among peers.

For communities such as Kirkholt, the challenge is not simply about policing but understanding why some young people feel the need to carry a weapon. Youth workers and charities frequently point to a combination of social pressures, fear of becoming a victim, exploitation by organised criminals, school exclusion, adverse childhood experiences and limited opportunities as factors that can increase vulnerability.

Greater Manchester Police has continued to target violent crime through proactive neighbourhood policing, stop-and-search powers where legally justified and intelligence-led operations against drug dealing and organised crime. Officers covering Balderstone and Kirkholt currently identify drug dealing, off-road bikes and wider neighbourhood crime as local priorities, with regular patrols aimed at disrupting criminal activity and reassuring residents.

There have also been encouraging signs across the borough. Greater Manchester Police says knife crime in Rochdale reduced during the second half of 2024 compared with the first six months of the year, while more than 100 knives were surrendered through permanent amnesty bins installed at local police stations. Officers say removing weapons from circulation is one part of a broader strategy to reduce serious violence.

Community organisations argue, however, that enforcement alone cannot solve the problem. Providing safe places for young people to spend time, investing in youth services, sports clubs and mentoring programmes, and creating better employment opportunities are all seen as essential to reducing the long-term appeal of gangs and weapon carrying.

Parents also have an important role. Talking openly about peer pressure, recognising changes in behaviour and encouraging children to seek help if they feel threatened can all help prevent situations from escalating. Schools across Greater Manchester continue to work alongside police and youth services to educate pupils about the devastating consequences of carrying knives, not only for victims but for those who choose to carry them.

For most people living in Kirkholt, knife crime is not something they encounter in everyday life. The vast majority of residents simply want safe streets, strong communities and opportunities for young people to succeed. Nevertheless, every incident involving a knife has the potential to leave lasting consequences for families and neighbourhoods.

Reducing knife crime ultimately depends on a combination of effective policing, early intervention and community support. While officers continue to target those involved in serious violence, many local organisations believe the greatest success will come from ensuring fewer young people ever feel the need to pick up a knife in the first place.

articles.title: Rochdale-born TikToker investigated by Scottish police over Meta smart glasses videos
articles.excerpt: A Rochdale-born TikTok creator known online as 'E Dobbin' is being investigated by Scottish police after complaints relating to videos recorded using Meta smart glasses.
articles.content_html:
Scott Margerison, a Rochdale native who publishes content online under the alias 'E Dobbin', is being investigated by Scottish police following complaints about videos allegedly recorded using Meta smart glasses during a trip around Scotland.

According to the Daily Record, officers are reviewing footage to determine whether any criminal offences have been committed. The reported videos include members of the public, retail staff and CalMac employees being recorded, along with confrontational interactions and footage from the bridge of the CalMac ferry Loch Seaforth. CalMac subsequently suspended public bridge visits.

Previous controversies

The Scotland investigation is not the first controversy surrounding Margerison's online activity. He previously attracted significant public criticism after uploading footage filmed inside JD Gym in which viewers alleged he made racist and sexually explicit remarks while recording members of the public. Reports at the time indicated he was subsequently banned from the gym.

Online content

Across multiple TikTok accounts, some of which are no longer available, Margerison has published videos promoting numerous conspiracy theories and alternative historical claims. These include the Tartaria conspiracy theory, claims that the Apollo Moon landings were faked, the so-called Kalergi Plan conspiracy theory, and claims that mountains are the fossilised remains of enormous petrified creatures.

The Kalergi Plan conspiracy theory has been widely rejected by historians and researchers and is commonly associated with antisemitic conspiracy narratives.

Many of Margerison's videos challenge established historical, archaeological and scientific consensus and have generated substantial debate and criticism online.

Police investigation

Scottish police have confirmed officers received complaints and are reviewing the available material to establish whether any criminal offences have been committed.

At the time of publication no criminal charges have been announced. An investigation does not imply criminal guilt.
